My teaching and professional experience spans **power systems, renewable energy, photovoltaics, electric circuits, engineering education, and electric-utility analytics**.

I have taught and supported engineering courses in both the United States and Colombia, ranging from introductory circuit analysis to senior- and graduate-level renewable energy courses. My teaching approach emphasizes connecting fundamental engineering principles with computational tools, real-world systems, and current challenges in the electric grid.

## University of Delaware

### Electrical Power Systems — ELEG 415/615
**Instructor · Spring 2027**

I am preparing and teaching ELEG 415/615, a senior- and graduate-level course in electric power systems.

The course develops the foundations of power-system analysis while connecting classical methods to modern grid challenges, including renewable generation, distributed energy resources, electrification, energy storage, and emerging large loads such as data centers.

Topics include power-system modeling, three-phase systems, transformers, transmission and distribution fundamentals, power flow, and the operation and control of modern electric grids.

My course design combines:

- Fundamental power-system theory
- Analytical problem solving
- Computational examples and engineering software
- Real-world grid applications
- Renewable and distributed energy integration
- Emerging power-system challenges

## Industry Experience

### Graduate Intern — Load Forecasting
**Dominion Energy · Glen Allen, Virginia · Summer 2026**

Worked with the Load Forecasting team in Electric Transmission on emerging and non-conforming electric load patterns.

My work included:

- Analyzing utility-scale load datasets
- Investigating data center load profiles
- Studying forecasting uncertainty associated with emerging electric loads
- Developing data-analysis and visualization workflows
- Translating analytical findings into insights relevant to utility planning and operations
- Collaborating with load forecasting engineers and planning stakeholders

This experience strengthened the connection between my academic work and practical power-system planning, particularly in the areas of large-load growth, data centers, grid demand, and forecasting.
